title: The Science of Exploitability: Decoding BlueHammer

artifacts.images: 22 original article figures downloaded; images.json records URLs and captions. Figures 8-12 inspected for native object paths, RPC identifiers, numeric DeviceIoControl code, symlink swap, and LSA registry access.
artifacts.code_blocks: No preformatted source listing. The inline code element contains the attack-chain arrow sequence. Actual code is in the decompiler/debugger screenshots; extracted text is code-blocks.txt.
verified_structure: WDUpdateDirectory object-manager alias; mpasbase.vdm symlink redirected to a VSS Windows/System32/config/SAM
OROpenHiveByHandle offline SAM access followed by SamiChangePasswordUser hash-authorized password replacement
artifacts.reconstruction: Three static source excerpts reconstruct Stages 5-7 in C++, Python ctypes, and Rust FFI. They are harness-dependent excerpts, not runnable complete exploits. Native attributes are constructed from the documented names; old/new hashes and worker state are harness inputs. Password decryption, full RPC procedure-42 invocation, and CloudFilter freeze are outside the excerpts. ORGetValue/OROpenKey are ordinary offline-registry API scaffolding for the SAM reads described by the article; they are not quoted source recovered from the original binary.

new_detection.race: Requires an actual batch DeviceIoControl call, NT object-manager symlink API, Defender update-object name, both update RPC identifiers, and a SAM hive path within 16 KiB. Ordinary update IPC or a numeric constant elsewhere cannot satisfy the rule.
new_detection.credential_access: Requires actual OROpenHiveByHandle and ORGetValue calls, SAM account subpath, SAM hive path, and SAMR password-change reference within 16 KiB. Describes co-occurrence, not proved data flow or runtime reachability.
new_detection.scope: Windows-specific APIs and target paths stay scoped to Windows. Call atoms support C/C++, C#, Go, Rust, Python and PowerShell; the verified samples cover C++, Python and Rust. These new operation rules cover source, not stripped native binary disassembly; the existing BlueHammer binary fingerprint remains available.
new_detection.independence: Neither new objective requires IHATEMICROSOFT, the hardcoded password, a chosen executable name, hash, GUID, or exact shadow-copy number.

corrections: Relocated Defender RPC UUID/endpoint references from privilege-escalation to communications/rpc; both are notable neutral IPC references. Broadened scope to source and scripts.

Replaced the generic Defender-plus-oplock hostile trigger with the targeted SAM alias-race objective, and updated its suite consumer. Removed redundant MsMpEng filename fragment; canonical defender-engine-process-reference remains.
Moved WDUpdateDirectory from family identity to a notable Defender object-name reference. Family identity now requires one of its two distinctive markers in addition to the RPC identifiers.
Renamed oplock symbolic-control reference for its actual match. Added same-call numeric/symbolic batch-oplock argument checks; numbers are matched by value, including hexadecimal and decimal.

Expanded the canonical SAM path matcher for escaped source separators. Moved the SAM account subpath into registry/keys/credential and allowed nested account paths in source; updated the managed parser consumer.

Moved shadow-copy registry-hive path to fs/path/filename-credential at notable; preserved its matcher, scope and log exclusion. Updated the explicit dump consumer. The broad web-served-loot consumer no longer treats a path-only observation as credential dumping; actual dump objectives remain eligible.

Moved offreg.dll name to fs/path/library without inherited write/persistence ATT&CK mappings; updated the hive-write context consumer. Offline open and value-read operations use registry/hive and registry/read respectively.

Audited the full communications/rpc leaf at its 100-rule budget. Relocated two misfiled HTTP observations (HTTP transport initialization and an HTTP RPC URL list) to their precise existing homes, preserving matchers, scope, severity, confidence and exact consumers. No RPC directory selectors were found. Placement-positive and near-miss controls pass.

indicators.binary_identity: Original unmodified FunnyApp.exe analyzed by Qualys. No source-package PURL is asserted.

excluded_feed_md5.reason: Article identifies it as the lab admin account NTLM/MD4 password hash, not a malicious file MD5.

indicators.clean_distribution: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=121721 downloads the genuine signed Defender package mpam-fex64.exe. It is used as an input to the exploit, not attacker-controlled infrastructure; excluded from ENDPOINTS.
indicators.lab_hosts: DESKTOP38, BlackHat2-CVE-2026-33825, NODE01 and dc60 are lab/validation machines, not hostile endpoints.
contextual_markers: WD is frozen and the new VSS can be used.
indicators.other_context: EICAR is a standard antivirus test string. The fixed Defender version is remediation context, not a malicious package. CVE-2026-33825 is vulnerability context.

verification.first_completed_detection_scan: All three original samples met the hostile floor immediately. Earlier analyzer invocations were blocked before analysis by rule-loading scope/budget/default errors; no below-floor sample was retried.
verification.fixture_reproduction: check.py materializes the eight controls in cleave fixtures, then checks them; this also restores them after an external checkout cleanup.
verification.facts: sample-facts.jsonl contains cleave facts for all three sources, including raw ASCII/UTF16 views, literals and call arguments. No parser errors. No encoded payloads are present; wide/escaped source literals were inspected alongside raw paths.
verification.static_syntax: Python ast.parse and Rust rustc --crate-type lib --emit metadata passed. C++ excerpt requires Windows headers/native harness and was not compiled on this macOS host.
verification.model_warning: Installed atomscan model spec v18 versus extractor v19; detection floors were measured from static trait findings, not ML scores.
commands: CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR=$PWD SCAN_NO_UPDATE=1 SCAN_HOPPER= atomscan --no-update --follow=none --mode slow --format json <article-testdata>
verification.final_required_gate: make validate, run as final action
verification.ancestor_review: ancestor-consumers.json records all old/new ancestor selectors. No communications/rpc directory consumers exist. HTTP-client ancestor consumers scoped to PE/C/JVM do not gain JavaScript matches; the script/multilanguage consumers still require their own browser, cookie-path or TLD evidence. HTTP transport initialization now correctly participates in HTTP capability selectors. The shadow-copy path stops satisfying broad credential-access selectors by itself; actual credential acquisition remains required. Broad filesystem/registry observation profiles retain their facility meaning.

omitted_behaviors: No new trait claims the CloudFilter wait, AES-CBC key derivation, token-to-session transfer, GUID service elevation, LSASS access or pass-the-hash from these excerpts. The article describes them, but these samples and new matchers do not establish them.
